body:
@Goodwine Thanks for working on this issue.

AFAIK the problem is on the compiler side - ie the compiler do not report the correct SourceSpan for the message:
- It reports `<source>.ts` when the template is in a separate file (ie `template.html`),
- It doesn't take into account the offset from the start of the ts file for inline template. The SourceSpan is reported as if the file is composed of the template only starting on line 1 column 1.

Both problems should be fixed and they should be independent of each other. Feel free to work on what is most important for you first.

The team is available to support you should you need. Thanks.

body:
After looking around, I don't think there's a problem with SourceSpan (I initially thought that too, but was not able to go forward), it seems like the html compiler doesn't read HTML files and instead it reads a string from the template which may or may not exist. Thankfully there is a previous process that normalizes the component metadata like: - if it has `template` -> set component TS file name as `templateUrl` - if it has `templateUrl` -> load HTML file and set contents as `template` Before normalization tho: ```js // ==== component with templateUrl === { "encapsulation": null, "template": null, "templateUrl": "./basic.html", "htmlAst": null, "styles": [], "styleUrls": [], "externalStylesheets": [], "animations": [], "ngContentSelectors": [], "interpolation": null, "isInline": false, "preserveWhitespaces": null } // ==== component with inline template === { "ngMetadataName": "Component", "changeDetection": 1, "selector": "basic2", "inputs": [], "outputs": [], "host": {}, "queries": {}, "template": "
\n

\n \n Welcome\n

" } ``` A way to deal with this could be storing the "template offset" in the template metadata, it would be 0 for loaded templates. Then consumers can choose to take this offset into account if they want.

## Current behavior XMB and XLIFF(1,2) print the wrong source line for a message in an inline template, [example in repo tests](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c8ad9657c9423cc2d07d6cc6a230ef28e2b60f3c/packages/compiler-cli/test/extract_i18n_spec.ts#L47): ```html src/comp2.ts:2,3 ``` 1. The compiler reads `@Component` and sets the value for `template` or `templateUrl`. 2. Then it normalizes things like this: ```js // not normalized { "template": "" } { "templateUrl": "foo.html" } // normalized { "template": "", templateUrl: "foo.ts" } { "templateUrl": "foo.html", template: "
bar
" } ``` 3. The compiler sends the value of `template` to an HTML compiler and gets back an AST. 4. The i18n extractor determines the position of the messages given the html AST. ## Expected behavior The generated code should have been: ```html src/comp2.ts:8,9 ``` 1. The compiler should store a value (e.g. `templateOffsetRows`) pointing to where in the TS file can the template be found. 2. Same behavior 3. Same behavior 4. Same as before, but the row/line numbers are incremented by `templateOffsetRows`. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions bazel test //packages/compiler-cli/test:extract_i18n ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? This is a follow up for issue #24884, tools that rely on the correctness of the output will be.. incorrect. This is IMO less important than the other bug because I expect most people to use html templates instead of inline templates in production. There are exceptions like tiny components, but in most cases those tiny components don't really have any messages to be translated. This is ofc on my experience. ## Environment Commit: c8ad9657
